analysis: Both supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4003-4494). The PR's only changed range is on the head side (3541-3575), a documentation-only addition about cluster service listeners following the cable and pairing. The supplied patch excerpt is truncated, so the full head text of that section was not visible. The excerpt describes ClusterService.listenerChange restarting or stopping the setup-exchange and control-lease listeners when the cable address or pairing changes, with a 5-second check interval. It compares pins, cluster label, link epoch and edge, never the edge secret, and an unreadable pairing store changes nothing. These claims are documentation only, with no code diff supplied. I found no security regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumption in the visible material. The base units cover unchanged GLM/Qwen tensor-parallel, prefix-cache SSD encoding and media text. They include the sealed all-sum, the load-agreement fail-closed binding and the SSD record encoding, which relate to T-041 (encrypted prefix tier, tenant partitions). Nothing there changed in this PR. Remaining questions for integration: (1) the actual listener restart logic in ClusterService.swift is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that documented behavior matches code. (2) An unreadable pairing store leaves a stale-pairing listener running, which the doc states is intentional, and which fails closed because stale-pairing handshakes are rejected. (3) The control lease listener restarts silently with no log line, a small observability gap but not a vulnerability. No finding is warranted from the evidence available.
